title: Greatest college football personalities? Finebaum reacts to being ranked ahead of Tebow, Saban
description: Tell us where they got it wrong.
fullText:
As we prepare to embark on yet another college football season, The Sporting News took a look at the 25 greatest college football personalities of all time.

Any college football fan will recognize the names. Some are coaches, while others are players. Broadcasters and media types populated the list, too.

"As someone who gets a little tired of college football lists, I must confess I found this one fairly fascinating," ESPN's Paul Finebaum told this reporter about being ranked No. 6 on the list right behind former Oklahoma linebacker Brian Bosworth and right in front of former Florida coach Steve Spurrier. "Being ranked ahead of Tim Tebow and Nick Saban in anything is a career bucket list."

Agree or disagree with the order of the list, but clearly most of these names belong here.

"The 'The Paul Finebaum Show' soared in popularity during the SEC's stranglehold of college football during the BCS and four-team College Football Playoff era," The Sporting News reads. "Finebaum's understated delivery, strong opinions and self-deprecating sense of humor rile up callers who stir the pot for arguments that often cross over into Big Ten country. It makes for some of the most entertaining material in the social-media era, and Finebaum continues to contribute to being the leading provocateur in the sport."

Broadcasters dominate the top of the list.

Former ESPN and "College GameDay" host Lee Corso comes in at No. 1 followed by the late "Pope of College Football" Beano Cook.

Former Mississippi State coach, the "Pirate" himself, the late Mike Leach ranks No. 4.

Rounding out the top 10: (7) Steve Spurrier, former Florida coach, (8) Lou Holtz, former coach and broadcaster, (9) Nick Saban, former coach and now broadcaster and (10) Tim Tebow, former player and now broadcaster.

Saban is one of two former Alabama coaches to make the list with Paul "Bear" Bryant listed at No. 12.

The Big Ten gets some love with former Ohio State coach Woody Hayes at No. 22.

Yes, we mentioned mascots. Oregon's duck Puddles (No. 24) and Georgia's Uga (No. 13) are on the list.

Check out the full list and tell us in the comment section what they got wrong and who was left out.

title: See where PFF ranked Zach Allen among NFL’s best interior linemen
description: Broncos star Zach Allen is one of the best IDL's in the NFL. Where should he be ranked?
fullText:
When the Denver Broncos signed Zach Allen to a three-year, $45.75 million deal in March 2023, the team got a great bargain.

Allen was selected in the third round of the 2019 NFL draft by the Arizona Cardinals, and while he was good there, he flew well under the radar. The Broncos knew they were getting a cornerstone piece for their defense. They knew they were getting a perfect fit for defensive coordinator Vance Joseph, who coached Allen with the Cards.

In three years, Allen has built on the success he started in Arizona and transformed into one of the league's best interior defensive linemen. He was selected as a first-team All-Pro last season while also making his first Pro Bowl.

However, when Gordon McGuinness of Pro Football Focus ranked the top interior defensive linemen in the league, Allen only came in at No. 10. Broncos fans are going to argue that is too low, and it probably is, but the league is stocked with some tremendous talent at this position.

"Allen's PFF grade has been pulled down some by his struggles against the run, but he's become one of the more reliable interior pass-rushers in football," McGuinness wrote for PFF. "He tallied 81 and 83 pressures in 2024 and 2025, and is coming off a 2025 season that saw him earn a career-high 76.6 PFF grade. His 50 combined sacks and quarterback hits in the regular season and playoffs last year were the most in the league."

It would be nice to see Allen earn a little more recognition here, but he is going to be one of the leaders of the Broncos' defense and one of the most difficult players for opposing offenses to deal with.

#Broncos DL Zach Allen: “We came close to the sack record last year. And we fully expect to break it this year.” pic.twitter.com/652koOZTPO

In three seasons with the Broncos, Allen has notched 20.5 sacks while placing pressure on the quarterback on seemingly every passing play. Last year, he also knocked down six passes at the line of scrimmage, adding a new wrinkle to his game. He had never had more than one in a season before that.

Prepared to begin his fourth season in Denver, the Broncos are happy they have Allen, and the list of players they'd prefer over him would likely be rather short.

title: Cardinals step up food game at State Farm Stadium. What's new for 2026
description: The NFL is back. And the Arizona Cardinals introduced over two dozen new foods for the season. See what you can order at State Farm Stadium in 2026.
fullText:
Football season is finally back. As the Arizona Cardinals get ready to gear up for the preseason, the culinary team geared up to showcase over two dozen new foods that will be available to guests at State Farm Stadium for the 2026 season.

Some of the most exciting new offerings include sweet maple bourbon chicken wings dipped in waffle dust, trendy Japanese-inspired milk bread sandwiches and customizable ice cream bars that guests can watch as they are hand dipped right in front of them.

In addition to all of the new offerings from Craft Culinary Concepts, celebrity chef Mark Tarbell has taken on an even bigger role with the Cardinals' food program after debuting his first in-stadium restaurant, Tarbell's Cha Cha Mouche, in 2025 alongside his bottled Cardinals-inspired wines. New in 2026 is a brand-new concept called Tarbell's Pizza.

"We dipped a little pinkie toe in the water last year with the tapas and wine bar at the club level and there was a lot for us to learn," Tarbell told The Republic. "I was excited, honored and scared, but because (the Cardinals) are so welcoming and supportive, we were able to grow from last year."

Here's a look at all of the new food options available at State Farm Stadium in 2026.

Craft Culinary Concepts is the primary food vendor responsible for concessions at State Farm Stadium.

New offerings for the 2026 season include:

Walkin' Tacos (Sections 126 and 434). Comes with your choice of Doritos Nacho Cheese Chips or Fritos topped with Tostitos nacho cheese sauce, taco meat, elote street corn and/or Tostitos vegetarian chili. Additional toppings include salsa, sour cream, shredded lettuce, shredded cheese and jalapeños. They can be made vegetarian or gluten-free with modifications.

Elote Streen Corn (Sections 126 and 434). Elote street corn garnished with cotija cheese, Tajin, cilantro and lime, served with a side of tortilla chips.

Copper State Cheesesteaks (Section 136). Made with shaved ribeye topped with grilled onions, poblano chiles, roasted poblano queso, shredded lettuce, diced tomato and shredded cheese, served on frybread.

Indian Frybread Dog (Sections 107, 129, 235, 247, 408 and 420). Hot Dog covered with chili, shredded cheese, shredded lettuce, diced tomato, crema and roasted jalapeño sauce served in a frybread bun.

Chicken and Waffle Wings (Sections 107, 129, 247, 408, and 420). Traditional bone-in chicken wings coated in waffle batter and topped with a maple bourbon glaze, served with french fries.

Arizona Chiltipin Honey Hot Chicken Breast Sandwich (Section 124). Fried chicken breast served on a brioche bun, dressed in lettuce, tomato, pickles and tanker sauce.

Big Red Turkey Wrap (Sections 103, 119, 125, 220, 406, 434, 437, 450 and 452). A Big Red tortilla filled with shaved smoked turkey breast, Crow's Dairy goat cheese spread, citrus dressed superfood slaw, smashed cucumber salad and superfood crunch (toasted hemp seeds, chia seed, pepita and nutritional yeast).

Spicy Super Protein Salad (Sections 103, 125, 220, 229). Little gem lettuce garnished with chile pequin grilled flank steak, hard-boiled egg, roasted vegetables, ancho chimichurri dressing and superfood crunch. Gluten-free.

Hand Dipped Ice Cream Bars (Section 137). Ice cream dipped in chocolate with several choices of toppings.

Several new food offerings are available only for those with tickets on the club level of the stadium.

Beef Birria Machete (Sections 210 and 240). Beef birria topped with Oaxaca and Menonita cheeses in an extra-large tortilla, served with diced red onions, cilantro, roasted tomato salsa, house made guacamole, crema, roasted jalapeño, Mexican onions, lime wedges and rich consommé.

Chopped Cheese Machete (Sections 210 and 240). Griddled ground beef in an extra-large tortilla dressed with diced onions, adobo seasoning and American cheese, topped with shredded lettuce, diced tomatoes and bodega sauce.

Red Dog Milk Toast Sandwiches (Section 229). Available in four flavors: bacon, egg and cheese dressed with chipotle kewpie mayo and chives; breaded mozzarella grilled cheese garnished with fresh basil pesto and "Sunday sauce" dip; Beef birria and Chihuahua cheese topped with diced red onion, cilantro, chipotle crema and consommé; and Dubai chocolate mousse sprinkled with candied pistachios, toasted kataifi and fresh strawberries. All served with homemade Kettle chips.

At every game, Craft Culinary Concepts will offer rivalry-inspired items at all Rivalry Grill locations, available in sections 129, 235 and 420. Executive chef Sean Kavanaugh said he took popular foods from the away team's home states and added an "Arizona twist."

Some examples for the 2026 season are:

Dallas Cowboys BBQ Brisket Burger (August 22). Made with a locally sourced, organic K4 Ranch beef patty, smoked brisket and pickles topped with jalapeño cowboy candy and barbecue sauce on a griddled brioche bun.

Seattle Seahawks Sonoran Style Seattle Dog (September 20). Comprises a bacon wrapped all-beef hot dog garnished with whipped cream cheese, griddled onions, roasted jalapeño sauce and yellow mustard, served on a brioche bun.

Tarbell's Pizza is located in the club level sections 209 and 240.

Classic Margherita Pizza – A Neapolitan-style pie with Tarbell's signature marinara sauce, creamy fresh mozzarella, fresh basil leaves and a drizzle of extra virgin olive oil on a crisp, thin crust. Vegetarian.

Soppressata Pizza – Tarbell calls it "the better pepperoni." Comprising thinly sliced crispy soppressata (spicy Italian dry-cured salami) layered over classic marinara sauce with melted mozzarella.

Crisp Korean-Style Chicken Pizza – Crispy fried chicken tossed in a savory soy glaze with bright lemon-butter, topped with tangy kimchi relish, shaved scallions, gochujang drizzle and fresh mozzarella.

Tar's BBQ Chicken Pizza – Tender chicken with a tangy lime-molasses BBQ sauce, charred tomato sauce, shaved red onion and fresh mozzarella.

title: Kendrick Bourne in line for key role in Cardinals offense
description: Trey McBride, Marvin Harrison Jr. and Michael Wilson might draw the Cardinals' headlines, but Kendrick Bourne should have a key role this season.
fullText:
Kendrick Bourne stood by his locker one day in training camp, his eyes gleaming and his smile spread wide.

The receiver was chatting about his role in the Arizona Cardinals' offense, one that has been widely ignored by fans and analysts alike. Their focus, understandably, has been on the Cardinals' biggest offensive stars: Trey McBride, Marvin Harrison Jr., Michael Wilson and Jeremiyah Love.

Bourne sits firmly under the radar.

"I'm like a secret weapon," Bourne said.

This, you see, is how he likes it.

"Those guys are gonna be in people's scouting reports," Bourne said. "I might be too, but it's not as eye-grabbing as those names. So that's where I fit in. I can go against a third DB. … And if I can go against that third corner that's coming in the game, I should be winning more than not."

And in Mike LaFleur's offense, Bourne has not been some forgotten player.

During eight days of 11-on-11 sessions in training camp, he caught 14 of 18 targets — slightly more than one in every 10 passes thrown by Jacoby Brissett. That might not make him a contender to lead the Cardinals in receiving, but it's a tangible role that could see him end the season with upwards of 60 targets.

"The way Mike has been drawing it up, it's been coming my way," Bourne said. "And it's not just because of me. It's where the ball's supposed to go."

That's despite his offseason move into a new role as the Cardinals' slot receiver. Last year in San Francisco, just 23.8% of Bourne's snaps came in the slot. The year before, in New England, that number was 22.4%. The last time more than 40% of his snaps were from the slot was back in 2019, his third season in the league.

His passing game coordinator for the 2019 season? Mike LaFleur.

"If you're gonna be able to play inside, you've gotta be able to match it up in the run game, and he has no problem doing that," LaFleur said. "He can get in there, he can block nickels, he can insert in the B gap if he needs to, he can do all those kinds of things."

So this offseason, when the Cardinals were in search of a slot receiver to fit LaFleur's scheme, they zeroed in on Bourne before handing him a two-year, $10 million contract in free agency.

And it's not just because of Bourne's physicality in the run game. Per Fantasy Points Data, Bourne created more separation when lined up in the slot than out wide, enabling him to earn more targets and yards per route run on those plays.

"It's so much more space in the slot," Bourne said. "It's actually better in my opinion. Cause I can go left and run all the way across. I can go in, go up and go back out. Outside, it's limited. It's a harder position."

Plus, Bourne is 31 now. The slot receiver is typically on the field in three-wide receiver sets. In his preseason appearance against the Raiders last week, that meant Bourne saw eight of 11 snaps with the starters. At his age, those small breathers are valuable.

"I should be feeling good and coming in with good energy," Bourne said. "And I think it's a good thing for where I'm at in my career, understanding that role, it's actually dope."

Bourne was careful to add a caveat here: If the game plan calls for a heavy snap count, or if one of the Cardinals' top two receivers goes down, he'll be ready. But on a lower workload, he believes his efficiency will be maximized.

That may not lead to 100 targets or 1,000 yards. Bourne wasn't brought here for gaudy numbers.

But in an offense predicated on run-pass conflict, in which the play of slot receivers is crucial, Bourne is, quietly, a crucial piece of the Cardinals' puzzle.

"He's been a great addition thus far," LaFleur said. "I love the energy he brings; I always have."

This article originally appeared on Arizona Republic: Kendrick Bourne in line for key role in Cardinals offense

title: Rams insider predicts who the team's WR3 will be in 2026
description: The Rams' WR3 role is anything but settled with weeks before the start of the 2026 season.
fullText:
The Los Angeles Rams' third wide receiver spot behind Puka Nacua and Davante Adams looks headed for a committee approach rather than a single clear winner, according to The Athletic's Nate Atkins.

The competition includes Konata Mumpfield, Jordan Whittington and Xavier Smith, with sixth-round rookie CJ Daniels also in the mix. None of the group has separated itself statistically.

Mumpfield, a seventh-round pick in 2025, finished his rookie season with 10 receptions for 92 yards and a touchdown across 17 games. Whittington posted 18 catches for 171 yards and no touchdowns in his second season, a step back from the 293 receiving yards he put up as a rookie in 2024. Smith caught 24 passes for 303 yards and doubled as the Rams' primary punt returner, logging 251 punt return yards last season. Daniels, while turning heads this offseason, is still just a rookie.

Atkins noted that "If the Rams wanted something more, I think they would have gone after a higher-octane receiver either in free agency, trades or the draft." There were rumors the Rams would draft USC receiver Makai Lemon at No. 13, but chose Alabama quarterback Ty Simpson instead. L.A. also reportedly "had eyes" on Ole Miss receiver De'Zhaun Stribling before the 49ers scooped him up at No. 33.

The lack of a standout and clear WR3 doesn't mean one doesn't exist, though. Atkins wrote that there will be "a couple of clear hierarchies" when it comes to the WR3 roles: "Mumpfield is the backup on the perimeter if Davante Adams were to get injured, and Whittington is the backup in an inside-outside role if Nacua were to get hurt."

He added that Whittington and Smith bring after-the-catch ability in different ways and will be active on game days largely because of their special teams value — provided Smith wins the punt return job outright entering the season. Additionally, Atkins believes the tight end position and role will also effectively serve as Matthew Stafford's third pass-catching option. The Rams have a few solid options, from Terrence Ferguson and Colby Parkinson to 2026 second-round pick Max Klare.

Nacua and Adams combined to dominate the receiving workload in 2025 — Nacua led the NFL with 129 catches for 1,715 yards and 10 touchdowns, while Adams led the league outright in touchdown catches with 14 on just 60 receptions. That leaves a thin slice of targets for whoever wins the No. 3 job, and Atkins expects the Rams to lean on specialization rather than a featured role.

title: Sophie Cunningham delivers perfect response after Toronto crowd boos Fever guard
description: Sophie Cunningham heard the boos during the Fever’s first trip to Toronto, but her clutch performance and gracious response afterward earned widespread praise.
fullText:
Sophie Cunningham delivers perfect response after Toronto crowd boos Fever guard originally appeared on The Sporting News. Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here.

Sophie Cunningham heard the boos as soon as she entered Tuesday's game against the Toronto Tempo. The Indiana Fever guard could have ignored the hostile reception or fired back at the crowd afterward. Instead, Cunningham offered a response that quickly earned praise from Fever fans.

"I want to shout out the Tempo crowd and the city," Cunningham said after Indiana's 101-95 victory, according to WNBA reporter Libaan Osman. "It's my first time being in Canada, but the crowd was absolutely amazing.

"I think that's what sports is all about. You're gonna get boos and you're gonna get cheers. But just the fact that they're so passionate, they're loud and they're putting on for the city, I think it's amazing."

Cunningham's praise stood out because some Toronto fans had booed her over previous comments regarding transgender athletes in women's sports. The 30-year-old never appeared rattled by the reception, however, and answered the hostility with one of her most important performances of the season.

Cunningham finished with 13 points, two rebounds and two assists off the bench. She made all three of her attempts from beyond the arc and went 4-for-5 at the free-throw line.

Sophie Cunningham on getting boos tonight in Toronto:

“The crowd was absolutely amazing. I think that’s what sports is all about. You’re going to get boos and you’re going to get cheers.” pic.twitter.com/m2KwevjtGi

Her biggest basket came with 1:25 remaining.

Toronto had spent the fourth quarter cutting into what had been a 17-point Indiana lead. Cunningham responded by burying a crucial 3-pointer that pushed the Fever's advantage back to 10 and temporarily halted the Tempo's comeback attempt. Toronto still managed to get within four points with 47 seconds remaining, but Indiana survived to secure its fifth consecutive victory.

Cunningham scored six points in the fourth quarter and provided exactly what the Fever needed on a difficult night for several of their biggest names. Caitlin Clark and Aliyah Boston combined to shoot only 2-for-10 from the field. Kelsey Mitchell, Indiana's leading scorer, also left the game with an injury during the third quarter and did not return for the final 10 minutes.

That placed additional pressure on the Fever's supporting cast. Cunningham embraced it.

"I'm just here," Cunningham said. "Whatever the team needs of me, I'm gonna do. That's what it's all about. Owning that. That's what it means to be the ultimate team pro."

MORE: Becky Hammon faces WNBA fine after fiery Aces ejection

Cunningham's comments about the Toronto crowd attracted almost as much attention as her clutch shooting. Fever supporters praised her for refusing to escalate the situation, with one fan writing, "Most WNBA players would be complaining and calling it hate. Sophie kills 'em with kindness."

Her response was consistent with the edge Cunningham has brought to Indiana. She does not shy away from confrontation, but she also understands the value of a passionate crowd, even when that crowd is rooting against her. Cunningham has given opposing fans plenty of reasons to be nervous this season. She is shooting 45.8 percent from 3-point range, the second-best mark in the WNBA, and has become one of Indiana's most dependable perimeter threats.

The Fever's victory moved them into third place in the standings and continued a five-game winning streak. More importantly, it showed Indiana can still find ways to close games when Clark and Boston struggle and Mitchell is unavailable.

Cunningham was booed when she stepped onto the floor. By the time she left it, she had delivered a clutch performance and a postgame response that was difficult to criticize.

title: SEC analyst reveals 'biggest reason' Oklahoma can win it all
description: David Pollack believes Oklahoma's championship hopes will ultimately depend on its quarterback's play.
fullText:
There is a lot of excitement in Norman ahead of the 2026 season as the Oklahoma Sooners are coming off a 10-3 year and a return to the College Football Playoff. The Sooners possess one of the best defenses in college football, as well as an offense returning a ton of talent, including quarterback John Mateer.

That's why many think this could be the best team in head coach Brent Venables' era. However, if Oklahoma is going to take the step many think it can and become a national championship contender, they are going to need more from Mateer and the offense.

In fact, college football analyst David Pollack said the Sooners' hopes for becoming a national championship contender will come down to Mateer's arm.

All of y'all in Norman, everybody's excited," Pollack said on the 'Dari Nowkhah Show' on KREF. "But they know that the biggest reason this team can be successful and win a national championship and go to the playoff again; it's going to be on that dude's arm."

The encouraging part for Oklahoma is that Mateer doesn't have to carry the entire team. The defense returns a significant amount of production, while the offense has added more weapons around him and returns several important contributors.

If Mateer can elevate the offense even a few levels, the Sooners could have the complementary football team necessary to make a serious run through the SEC and into the College Football Playoff.

That's ultimately why Pollack's point carries so much weight: Oklahoma appears to have the defense, talent and experience needed to contend. Whether it becomes a national championship team could come down to how far Mateer's right arm can take it.

title: People around NBA believe Lakers can't build front office until sold
description: There is a belief around the NBA that the Lakers cannot continue to build out their front office until their ownership situation is resolved.
fullText:
After Mark Walter officially bought a majority share of the Los Angeles Lakers this past October, he began the process of modernizing how the franchise is run. A number of people were hired to important front office positions, and fans started to feel optimistic about the direction the team was headed.

But that process is now in flux after Walter agreed to sell that majority stake to Josh Kushner and Bob Iger last week. To add even more uncertainty to the whole situation, five of the six Buss siblings voted to sell their remaining 17.8% share in the Lakers to Kushner and Iger on Monday.

Although Ramona Shelburne of ESPN said that the process of mirroring how the Los Angeles Dodgers, the Major League Baseball team Walter owns, run things will continue for now, another report indicated that the progress the front office has made may be halted. Dan Woike of The Athletic wrote that the belief around the NBA is that the Lakers cannot continue to hire people for important positions until their ownership situation is resolved.

"According to a pair of league sources who spoke on the condition of anonymity because they are not authorized to publicly discuss the Lakers' internal operations, there is a belief around the NBA that the team cannot complete the buildout of its basketball operations department until the ownership situation is resolved. After laying out a vision for a pair of assistant general managers, with one focused on analytics and one focused on player scouting, the team has yet to make any inroads in pro scouting. With preseason games set to start in a little more than a month, filling a staff and getting everyone accustomed to a system was already going to be difficult. Now it feels like a distant hope more than a reality."

In recent months, Los Angeles had hired Tony Bennett, a four-time ACC Coach of the Year who coached the University of Virginia to the national championship in 2019, to be a draft advisor. Rohan Ramadas, who was described as a "literal rocket scientist" by one source, was also brought in to be an assistant general manager and focus on analytics and the salary cap.

A number of other people were hired to handle different roles in both the basketball and business side of the organization after Walter's purchase went through.

Iger told the California Post late last week that it is "premature to speculate" on any possible plans as far as hires or changes.

This article originally appeared on LeBron Wire: People around NBA believe Lakers can't build front office until sold

title: Raiders' Kirk Cousins blasts Maxx Crosby & Texans for rough NFL preseason physicality
description: Kirk Cousins had a stern reminder for the Raiders, Texans, and Maxx Crosby amid the physicality he faced during their NFL preseason matchups.
fullText:
Raiders' Kirk Cousins blasts Maxx Crosby & Texans for rough NFL preseason physicality originally appeared on The Sporting News. Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here.

NFL Preseason is typically when the physicality ramps up. Defenses are more eager to simulate their full strength against receivers, tight ends, and quarterbacks. There are obviously upsides to this, but Kirk Cousins doesn't seem to appreciate it when some players go over the line a bit. In the past few weeks, he has called for certain players and teams to chill out a bit since the games do not count yet. The Las Vegas Raiders, Houston Texans, and even Maxx Crosby got blasted after the veteran quarterback had enough.

Week 1 of the 2026 NFL season is around the corner. Plenty of teams are practicing the schemes they formulated in the offseason and starting to turn the dial up on execution. Kirk Cousins understands that, but he made a plea to a lot of squads he was facing. He asked them to calm down a bit when taking him down.

Cousins specifically asked Maxx Crosby, the rest of the Raiders defense, and the Texans not to be too harsh with his arm. The 14-year veteran wants to stay on the field for a long time, and all this roughness during the NFL Preseason does not seem to be helping, via Adam Hill of The Las Vegas Review-Journal.

"My elbow got hit. I joke with Maxx, and I say, 'You can touch me anywhere you want, just don't touch my arm.' You want to bump me in the ribs? Fine. I think if anything, hitting me in the hips or the ribs is actually good because it simulates what I need to feel. I've got some scars from some hits in real games where helmets go into armpits and things, and it ruins your season. So, I was just asking Crosby to just stay off the arm, and I had to remind the Texans as well," the Raiders quarterback declared.

Notably, Cousins sustained a shoulder injury back in the 2024 NFL season. Since then, his numbers haven't been the best. During his last two years with the Atlanta Falcons, he also got sacked 41 times. At one point, the quarterback even led the league with 16 interceptions back in 2024 because of how bad his arm situation was.

"I might as well just take the red jersey off because you're playing with, sometimes, an understood rule that if it's not understood, then what are we doing?" Cousins added.

The Raiders quarterback does have a point here. He did wear a jersey, which meant that the no-contact rule was in place during their NFL preseason joint practices and drills. Yet, Crosby, the Raiders defense, and the Texans were all still fairly rough in taking him down. It all came to a head when Crosby and Cousins had to be benched from team drills a few weeks back.

Hopefully, this plea to the Raiders and other defenses would help Cousins and the other quarterbacks during the NFL Preseason. It's one thing to have their season cut short during the 17-game campaign, but not getting to experience it all after a lengthy offseason is a different kind of bummer.

title: Sports tech company Rule42 invests in AUSL, acquires Softball America
description: Rule42 — a new sports tech company founded by former Intel president Renée James — is investing in AUSL and has acquired Softball America.
fullText:
As the parent of Major League Baseball prospect, Renée James got a first-hand look at how chaotic, strenuous and inaccessible the scouting process could be for a young athlete aiming to land a college scholarship or a professional contract.

The former president of the Intel Corporation, who then also founded and sold Ampere Computing, thought to herself: "We can do better."

"There's no scouting for women. The men scouting for amateur (sports) is very pay-to-play," James told USA TODAY Sports. "It is such a rough path that I thought, you know, use your power for good, you could make this better for a lot of kids who didn't make it who could have gotten college scholarships."

So, a few weeks ago, James launched Rule42 — a sports technology company aiming to modernize the discovery process for athletes, scouts and teams.

And softball is the sport that Rule42 is jumping into first with both feet.

Rule42 announced on Wednesday, Aug. 18 that it is making a significant investment in the Athletes Unlimited Softball League, which just completed its second full season. Alongside MLB, the Milwaukee Brewers, Ryan Sanders Baseball and Athletes Unlimited, the Rule42 Sports Group will be among the league's largest investors. James will also join the AUSL's Board of Directors.

Additionally, Rule42 has acquired Softball America, one of the leading digital publications that covers all levels of the sport with editorial news and prospect rankings. Softball America's top 150 prospect rankings for the high school class of 2028 debuted on Rule42's website on Tuesday.

Softball America will become "Softball America by Rule42" and the entirety of the digital publication's team will be employed by James' company. Tara Henry, the general manager of Softball America, is also now the Vice President of Softball at Rule42.

"The idea is to make (Rule42) pretty synonymous with what we're doing and just continue to grow the game from the youth market to the college market, all the way to the pro market," Henry told USA TODAY Sports. "Marrying the tech side and the sports side, it was a no-brainer for us. I'm just really excited that we'll be able to give more athletes opportunities beyond the Power Four, beyond the mid-majors, and really find places to develop and grow talent."

Softball America's rankings will be free to access on Rule42's website, while it will still publish subscriber-only editorial content on the On3 network.

Rule42 is self-funded by James and plans to build an AI-powered technology platform that gives athletes an equal shot at being discovered by college and pro scouts. The service will be free to use for athletes and parents.

The genesis for starting Rule42 came from James watching other parents struggle to get their kids noticed as she was seeing her son Ryan become an MLB prospect who was drafted in the third round this year by the Toronto Blue Jays out of the University of Oregon.

And then James discovered that the process is even tougher for women.

"It's more than hard. It's heartbreaking. These parents are taking second mortgages on their homes. For the women, you have to go to a college program to become a pro," James said. "There's no formal scouting. There isn't the infrastructure for women. So, for women, we can leapfrog the decades of the scouting structure that there is for men by using technology.

"And now there are major scholarships for girls that we need to match them with. These coaches in these programs do not have time to find all the talent out there."

What James is referring to was a domino that fell with the landmark House v. NCAA settlement in 2025 which eliminated sport-specific scholarship caps. It more than doubled the possible number of athletic scholarships that can be offered to women at the Division I level. Previously, many softball programs — and other women's college sports teams — didn't have the full complement of scholarships that matched their roster sizes.

With its investment in AUSL, Rule42 will have a footprint at all levels of softball, a sport that has a growing audience.

This year's Women's College World Series smashed viewership records for ESPN as it was the most watched WCWS on record, drawing an average of 1.6 million viewers per game. And for the AUSL, ABC drew an average audience of 732,000 viewers for Game 1 of its championship series this year, making it the most-watched professional softball game on record.

All of that is building toward the sport making its return to the Olympics in 2028 on American soil.

"We're incredibly excited to have Renée on board as an investor," Jon Patricof, CEO of Athletes Unlimited, told USA TODAY Sports. "She is one of the most accomplished, experienced and successful executives in the technology industry. She is someone who is going to offer us so much, and has already offered so much advice and guidance on how to build a large, scalable business."

With Kim Ng as its commissioner, merchandise sales for the AUSL increased by 110% this season and social media impressions grew by 97%. Year-over-year television viewership grew by more than 150% as the AUSL had more than 90 games distributed across ESPN platforms, CBS Sports Network and MLB Network this season.

"It's a very positive opportunity," James said. "There are girls everywhere playing softball and they wonder, what comes next? And now, the answer is they can be a pro too, and that is why I'm investing in AUSL. I want to see us grow. I want to see us continue."

Athletes Unlimited announced last month that it was pausing play in its women's basketball and volleyball leagues. But Patricof made it clear the organization is all-in on softball.

"We've had so much success with softball. We've significantly expanded our footprint over the last two years in that sport," Patricof said. "In basketball and volleyball, our thoughts are we want to up the trajectory of what we're achieving with softball. If we're going to go forward in either of those sports, it's going to be in a big and meaningful way, and so, we're exploring a host of opportunities.

"But for now, softball has become far and away the largest part of the Athletes Unlimited portfolio. We're just coming off an amazing season and we're ready for 2027."

This article originally appeared on USA TODAY: Sports tech company Rule42 invests in AUSL, acquires Softball America

title: Dan Campbell Reveals Major Change to His Legendary Coffee Habit
description: Detroit Lions coach Dan Campbell revealed that recent blood work prompted him to make some health changes, including cutting back on his famous caffeine intake.
fullText:
Dan Campbell is still attacking his mornings the way Detroit Lions fans would expect, but the head coach has apparently made at least one significant adjustment to his legendary daily routine.

During a recent exclusive interview, Campbell revealed that he continues to work out every morning, but some recent blood work convinced him to make a few changes to his health routine. One of those changes involved something closely associated with the Lions coach over the years: caffeine.

"I still work out every morning," Campbell said during the interview.

That part hasn't changed. His coffee intake, however, apparently has.

Campbell explained that someone within the organization encouraged him to have blood work done to get a better picture of what was happening with his body.

"Our guy Fish told me, 'Why don't you take this blood test? They'll check all your levels, vitamins, hormones and all that stuff,'" Campbell said. "A couple of little things came out of it. I changed a couple of things."

Campbell didn't get into the specifics of everything that changed, but he did confirm one adjustment.

"Yes, I did back down on caffeine," Campbell said.

Considering Campbell's well-documented relationship with coffee, that sounded like a pretty dramatic lifestyle change.

Apparently, "cutting back" means something slightly different when you're Dan Campbell.

"It's not a gallon," Campbell joked. "It's half a gallon now. We're good."

So much for switching to herbal tea.

Even more remarkable is how late Campbell says he can continue drinking coffee without it interfering with his sleep. When asked how long his caffeine habit stretches into the day, Campbell admitted, "Most of the time, it goes well into the evening."

For most people, that would be a recipe for staring at the ceiling until 3 a.m. Campbell apparently isn't most people.

"I'm one of those weird people," Campbell said. "I can chug a cup of coffee right before I go to bed, and I'm out cold. It doesn't keep me up."

That might be the most Dan Campbell answer imaginable.

Campbell's morning workouts aren't going anywhere, and neither is his coffee.

The Lions coach simply appears to be paying a little more attention to what his body is telling him after getting detailed blood work done. That led him to make a few unspecified adjustments and, yes, actually reduce his caffeine consumption.

Of course, Campbell's idea of cutting back still involves joking about drinking half a gallon of coffee and having no problem downing a cup shortly before bed.

Some habits are harder to break than others.

And with Campbell, apparently caffeine isn't keeping him awake anyway.

title: Official | Freiburg extend with record-setting Vincenzo Grifo
description: SC Freiburg have officially confirmed another contract extension for club record-holder Vincenzo Grifo. As usual, the Breisgau club did not disclose the precise length of the new agreement. For Grifo,...
fullText:
SC Freiburg have officially confirmed another contract extension for club record-holder Vincenzo Grifo. As usual, the Breisgau club did not disclose the precise length of the new agreement. For Grifo, another agreement continues a relationship that has long since moved beyond that of a conventional senior player.

The Italian international has accumulated 360 competitive appearances for Freiburg, placing him fourth on the club's all-time list. His 108 goals and 98 assists are both club records. Those marks have fallen in relatively quick succession. Grifo surpassed Nils Petersen as Freiburg's record Bundesliga goalscorer. He then drew level with Petersen's all-competitions scoring record in March before breaking it during a memorable Europa League victory over Genk.

Despite having already secured his place in club history, Grifo insists that his ambitions remain intact.

"The journey isn't over yet and I've still set myself a few goals," Grifo said following confirmation of the extension. "I'm still very ambitious and want to be on the pitch in every game. The competition from the younger lads motivates me and makes all of us better."

Sporting director Klemens Hartenbach emphasized that Grifo's value extends well beyond his production on the pitch.

"Working with Vince is something special," Hartenbach said. "With his consistently strong sporting performances and his role as someone others can turn to, he is incredibly important for the entire group."

title: Injured Arsenal player could return to training this week
description: Injured right-back Jurrien Timber could return to full first-team training with Arsenal this week, according to a report.Photo via Arsenal on TwitterAlex Howell reports for the BBC that while William ...
fullText:
Alex Howell reports for the BBC that while William Saliba will be out of action for a few months, Jurrien Timber could return to first-team training this week.

That would certainly be a boost for Arsenal, with Ben White the only natural senior right-back in the squad at the moment. Cristhian Mosquera can fill in on the right, but with Saliba out, Mosquera is needed centrally.

Mikel Arteta has been turning to youth players throughout pre-season, but even then, he's often needed to play youngsters out of position. Right-back isn't Arsenal's strongest academy position right now.

The current defensive injury situation at Arsenal is part of the reason the club are looking to invest in a new signing in the position, with a deal for Ezri Konsa now close. But Timber's return would also help.

While White is fit, Arsenal aren't in a bad situation. The Gunners only have one game a week for the remainder of August, so rotation shouldn't be a necessity until the transfer window closes.

But White himself is only recently back from a knee injury, and he's struggled with various fitness problems over the last couple of years.

Arsenal certainly won't want to go into September relying entirely on White for all the Premier League, Champions League, and League Cup matches that month.

Indeed, if Timber returns to full fitness and Konsa joins, Arsenal may even consider selling White before the deadline.

James Olley reported as much for ESPN recently, writing that White could be allowed to depart if the Gunners pursue a deal for Konsa.

But until Timber is fit, it's simply too much of a risk. Adding Konsa, losing White, and still missing Timber would leave Arsenal still relying completely on one player for four competitions. So it's important they get the Dutch international back.

title: Analysis: Excitement could build if Lions beat Norwich
description: Analysis of Millwall's positive start to the 2026-27 season from BBC Radio London's Phil Parry.
fullText:
It was a gut-wrenching experience for Millwall to get so close to promotion last season.

Head coach Alex Neil was distraught. Everyone was really gutted. You wonder: how is the hangover going to be cured?

Well, with a little bit of freshening up and the experience Alex has got, I think he has just dealt with it and they've got back on the horse.

When you consider that Millwall have got some injuries as well, to get a win on Saturday against Bristol City, a team who have got ambition themselves, was a really good performance.

Neil knows the expectation this year is to get back into the play-offs. It goes to eight teams this season; I think they should be fine.

Transfer business isn't necessarily done yet. They won't sell Femi Azeez, who has been linked with Brighton & Hove Albion and Hull City, unless the bid meets what is quite a decent valuation; but if they do, they might bring some players in as a consequence of that.

On Saturday, they play Norwich, who have been tipped to do very well this season. They finished like a train last season under Philippe Clement.

It's the first game at The Den, an early kick-off, and everyone's going to be up for it. It's going to be a much-anticipated game against another challenger.

If Millwall come out of this with six points from these first two games, I think, genuinely, excitement will start to build.

title: BMW Championship 2026: My pick to play Player of the Year spoiler
description: Editor's Note: This article is published in partnership with Read The Line, a Golf Digest content partner.
fullText:
Only 50 players left standing on the PGA Tour are headed to St. Louis, where the second leg of the FedEx Cup playoffs awaits as players descend on Bellerive Country Club for another high-stakes test. While Memphis asked players to play under control and find fairways, this golf course looks to emphasize power and should give an advantage to those with a little extra horsepower off the tee.

Since Bellerive last hosted the PGA Championship in 2018, they have lengthened six holes, stretching the par-70 layout to 7,448 yards. That's a long course, and while the most correlated stat to success is always approach play, I am using carry distance as a way to separate the favorites. The rough is set to be thick but manageable, which opens up the opportunity to deploy a bomb-and-gauge strategy.

The entire field is also a bit more on edge headed into this week after being decimated by Scottie Scheffler in Memphis by eight shots. The boogeyman is back, and rest assured, he's the most intimidating player on the planet when he has his A-game. The bigger storyline is the top-30 cutline after this week. Just over half the field will leave St. Louis with a ticket to East Lake and the Tour Championship.

Here are my top-10 contenders to win the 2026 BMW Championship.

There is an enormous gap between the Wyndham Clark that we saw at the beginning of the season and the one we are watching now. He won his second U.S. Open at Shinnecock in June, owns five top-five finishes across his last 10 starts, and just added another T-5 in Memphis after closing with 68.

We know that Clark possesses plenty of speed and loves golf courses where aggressive driving is rewarded. He has demonstrated that his ceiling rises when in proper form, and the test this week should fit his eye.

Read The Line's Joe Idone and John Haslbauer make the case for Viktor Hovland at the 2026 BMW Championship:

Watch Read The Line's full betting breakdown of the 2026 BMW Championship here.

He's starting to look like Ludvig Aberg again. A quiet T-7 last week in Memphis included rounds of 65 and 67 providing late-season optimism. Now he moves onto a golf course that should allow his elite driving ability to become a much larger part of the conversation.

The extra 10-15 yards off the tee that he gains will compound over 72 holes and leave him with much more manageable approach distances. His baseline raises on courses like Bellerive, so he could be a sneaky pick to win the BMW Championship.

What he lacks in pure power, Matt Fitzpatrick more than makes up for with elite approach play. He leads the field in strokes gained/approach and from a ball-striking perspective, he aligns perfectly with what I expect from Bellerive.

He's currently second in the FedEx Cup standings, owns three victories this season and added another steady T-12 in Memphis. Nothing about his summer feels accidental anymore. This is a player who has proven to be a contender every week, no matter the golf course.

Even though the host venue rotates every year, there is something about the way that the BMW Championship sets up their golf courses that fits the eye of Viktor Hovland. He found something late in the season with his iron play that has kickstarted his success and allowed him to capture another PGA Tour victory at the Travelers Championship.

A T-32 in Memphis isn't going to generate much hype coming into the week. I'm OK with that. Hovland's game makes considerably more sense to me at Bellerive, where the premium shifts away from simply finding fairways and toward surviving long approach after long approach. His skills will be properly rewarded.

There is always the temptation to overlook Tommy Fleetwood based on win equity, but we're talking about a short field and the playoffs! Fleetwood arrives playing some of the most consistent golf of anyone on Tour. His T-7 in Memphis last week was his eighth top-10 of the season.

His game is so well-rounded that you cannot write him off anywhere. The harder the course plays, typically the better for Fleetwood. He answered the big question we all wondered in East Lake last year. Now can he do it in a field of 50? I think there is reason to trust backing him in St. Louis.

This season has not exactly produced fireworks for Team Schauffele. But there is reason to believe in a strong finish after consecutive great results from Xander heading into this week. He has always been one of those players who can quietly check every box without necessarily leading the tour in any one category.

He's one of the best in the field in par-4 scoring and long iron approach proximity, two highly sought-after traits at Bellerive. The win has not arrived in 2026 … yet. Expect Schauffele to be in the mix.

What happened in Memphis was a tough look. Rory McIlroy looked completely out of sync and under-prepared. McIlroy finished 66th out of 69 players, 25 shots behind Scheffler, and openly admitted afterward that he felt lost with his swing. It was ugly. There really isn't another way to frame it.

This is a new week. If I could build a prototype player specially for Bellerive, they would look a lot like McIlroy. I'm respecting the warning signs he showed of potentially being uncommitted, making him No. 4 in my rankings, but if things suddenly kick start into gear then Rory can outrace everyone in the field.

At some point, Sam Burns has to win one of these things again. Only Scottie Scheffler has played better golf over the past three months, and Burns has been in contention week after week since coming painfully close to victory at the U.S. Open.

Taking into account the incredible form and considering the course fit, he should be on everyone's short list. Burns has been remarkably steady from tee-to-green and possesses that type of putting acumen that will soon ultimately push him across the finish line to victory. That might just happen this week.

Outside of the obvious player at No. 1, there is not a player in the field who makes more statistical sense at Bellerive than Cameron Young. He's got all the tools, which includes averaging 317 yards off the tee, which will prove to be a massive head start on the golf course.

We're talking about a player who has already won The Players and the Cadillac Championship this season. He's burst down the door and now understands exactly what it takes to secure a trophy. I can't find a better course fit than Cam Young, and I fully expect him to make a charge and potentially cement his case for PGA Tour Player of the Year with another win.

Last week was a not-so-gentle reminder: When Scottie Scheffler is holing putts, nobody stands a chance. Unsurprisingly, he checks all the boxes for Bellerive. The question we have to ask ourselves is if the putter is merely average, can he still win?

A 50-player field technically makes that less difficult. This is a golf course that should allow him separation, and the No. 1 player in the world is also the No. 1 player in the rankings for very good reason. He sits back atop the throne and has his heart set on sweeping the playoffs.

Joe Idone is a Read The Line contributor and host of the Preferred Lines podcast.

title: Watch: Padres' Fernando Tatis Jr. robs grand slam, homers twice vs. Mets
description: Fernando Tatis Jr. homered twice and performed an immaculate grand slam robbery to help the San Diego Padres beat the New York Mets in Flushing, N.Y.
fullText:
Aug. 19 (UPI) -- Fernando Tatis Jr. homered twice and performed an immaculate grand slam robbery to help the San Diego Padres beat the New York Mets in Flushing, N.Y.

The All-Star outfielder homered in the first and fifth innings of the 5-2 triumph Tuesday at Citi Field. He stole a would-be grand slam from shortstop Francisco Lindor in the bottom of the second.

"He doesn't just do it," Padres manager Craig Stammen told reporters. "He does it with a flair."

The Padres, who have won eight of their last 10 games, remain in the lead for the third wild card slot. They hold a two game lead on the Arizona Diamondbacks for the National League's final playoff ticket.

Tatis started his exploits by hitting the first pitch of the night to left field for a 452-foot home run. The Mets attempted to rally in the bottom of the next inning. Padres starter Robbie Ray started the frame with walks issued to designated hitter Francisco Alvarez and first baseman Christopher Morel. Second baseman Marcus Semien flew out in the next at-bat.

Ray proceeded to walk left fielder A.J. Ewing to load the bases. Lindor walked to the plate two at-bats later. He watched a Ray changeup miss the zone for a ball. He then smacked a 1-0 sinker deep to right field.

Tatis watched the ball cruise 337 feet toward the right field corner. He left his feet over the warning track and reached his gloved left hand high over the wall before snagging the ball. Tatis landed and celebrated the catch by flipping the ball out of his glove and into his right hand.

He returned to the plate in the top of the fifth to face Mets starter Zac Thornton for a third time. The Padres slugger unloaded on a 2-1 fastball, sending the pitch to right center for a 379-foot, two-run blast.

Catcher Luis Torrens hit a 417-foot solo shot for the Mets' first run to lead off the bottom of the fifth. Padres first baseman Ty France responded with an RBI single in the top of the seventh.

Center fielder Luis Robert Jr. drove in the Mets' final run with a 390-foot solo shot in the bottom of the eighth. Padres third baseman Manny Machado hit a 397-foot solo homer in the top of the ninth for the game's final run.

Ray allowed just three hits and one run over six innings to improve to 11-7 this season. Thornton surrendered six hits and three runs over five innings to drop to 3-4.

Tatis went 2 for 5 with three RBIs, two runs scored and a strikeout. He hit .280 with 15 home runs, 28 stolen bases and 60 RBIs through his first 125 games this season.

The Padres (68-59) remain in second place in the National League West, eight games behind the division-leading Los Angeles Dodgers (76-51).

The Mets (57-70) remain in last place in the National League East, 17.5 games behind the division-leading Atlanta Braves (74-52).

title: Nick Kyrgios suspended after positive cocaine test: 'I'm deeply disappointed in myself'
description: Nick Kyrgios confirmed the suspension, saying he made "a huge mistake."
fullText:
Tennis star Nick Kyrgios was suspended by the International Tennis Integrity Agency (ITIA) after one of his samples came back positive for cocaine, the agency announced Wednesday.

Kyrgios tested positive for benzoylecgonine, a metabolite of cocaine, in a sample he provided at the ATP 250 event in Mallorca, Spain on June 22. Cocaine is among the drugs banned by the World Anti Doping Agency (WADA).

Kyrgios, 31, confirmed the suspension in a message on Instagram, saying he made "a huge mistake."

A portion of that message read:

"I'm sorry to my fans, my family, my sponsors and everyone close to me. Above all, I'm sorry to the kids who follow me. I know the example this sets and I'm deeply disappointed in myself."

In his statement, Kyrgios said he didn't want to make excuses for his behavior, but noted that coming to terms with the possible end of his career has been difficult. He said injuries have prevented his body from doing "what my mind expects it to do."

He said the positive test has given him a wake-up call, and that he will spend the next month off social media while "getting myself right."

In the ITIA statement, it noted that Kyrgios has the ability to appeal the suspension, but has not done so yet. While suspended, Kyrgios is unable to play in or coach "any events organized or sanctioned by World Tennis, WTA, ATP, the Grand Slams, or any national association."

Kyrgios peaked at No. 13 on the ATP rankings back in 2016. While he showed promise early in his career, he seemed to hit his stride in 2022, when he reached the finals at Wimbledon. There, Kyrgios lost to Novak Djokovic. He appeared undeterred by that lose, reaching the quarterfinals in his next Grand Slam.

But injuries struck at the end of the year. Since then, Kyrgios has battled various ailments during his recovery. Since the 2022 U.S. Open, Kyrgios has appeared in just one Grand Slam, the 2025 Australian Open, where he fell in the first round.

Due to his inactivity as a result of injuries, Kyrgios ranked 899th at the time of his suspension.

title: Angel Reese makes wild WNBA history with latest 400-rebound season
description: Angel Reese became the second-fastest player in WNBA history to reach 400 rebounds in a season, but the player ahead of the Dream star is remarkably familiar.
fullText:
Angel Reese makes wild WNBA history with latest 400-rebound season originally appeared on The Sporting News. Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here.

Angel Reese continues to make rebounding history, and the only player standing between the Atlanta Dream star and another WNBA record is Reese herself. Reese became the second-fastest player in league history to collect at least 400 rebounds in a single season during Atlanta's 97-82 victory over the Las Vegas Aces on Tuesday. She reached the milestone in her 34th game of the 2026 season.

The record belongs to Reese, who secured her 400th rebound in only 32 games during her historic rookie season with the Chicago Sky in 2024. That means the two fastest 400-rebound seasons in WNBA history belong to the same player.

Reese did much more than chase a milestone against Las Vegas. She finished with 21 points, 10 rebounds, four assists and four steals in 39 minutes, helping Atlanta improve to 22-13. She shot 6-for-13 from the field, made her only 3-point attempt and converted eight of nine free throws. ESPN reported that it was her league-leading 24th double-double of the season.

Reese's 400th rebound offered another reminder of how quickly she has separated herself from nearly every other rebounder in WNBA history. The former LSU star entered the league with questions surrounding how her game would translate against bigger and more experienced frontcourt players. She answered those questions almost immediately.

Angel Reese is the 2nd fastest player in WNBA history to reach 400+ rebounds in a season.

Behind only herself in 2024. pic.twitter.com/C2eSpD5Hbg

Reese averaged 13.1 rebounds as a rookie and became the fastest player in WNBA history to reach 400 rebounds, accomplishing the feat in 32 games. She finished that season with 446 boards despite appearing in only 34 games. After another dominant rebounding season in 2025, Reese was traded from Chicago to Atlanta in April. The Dream sent their 2027 and 2028 first-round picks to the Sky while also acquiring the right to swap second-round selections in 2028.

The significant price has looked justified. Reese is averaging approximately 12 rebounds per game in 2026 and has helped turn Atlanta into one of the Eastern Conference's strongest teams. Her offensive game also has expanded, with the 24-year-old averaging nearly 16 points while continuing to control the paint.

MORE: Becky Hammon faces WNBA fine after fiery Aces ejection

Tuesday's performance was especially important after Atlanta suffered a painful 95-91 overtime loss to Caitlin Clark and the Indiana Fever on Sunday. Reese recorded 15 points, 14 rebounds and six assists in that game, but missed a potential game-winning putback at the end of regulation. Two nights later, she responded with an efficient 21-point double-double against one of the league's top teams.

Rhyne Howard led Atlanta with 23 points, while Reese's work on both ends helped the Dream pull away for a convincing road win. Her four steals matched her scoring and rebounding production with another display of defensive activity. Reese also reached 1,000 career rebounds earlier this season, becoming the fastest player in league history to hit that mark. She did it in her 79th career game, surpassing Tina Charles' previous record by 10 games, according to ESPN.

Individual records have followed Reese since she entered the league, but the circumstances are different now. She is no longer compiling historic numbers for a struggling Chicago team. Reese is producing at that level for an Atlanta group positioned to make a serious playoff run. Reaching 400 rebounds once is an extraordinary accomplishment. Reese has now done it twice in three seasons, and she owns both of the fastest runs to that milestone.

At this point, Reese is not simply chasing WNBA rebounding history. She is competing against her own records.

title: Isabelle Harrison starts for Tempo against Fever
description: Former Lady Vol Isabelle Harrison starts for Toronto against Indiana.
fullText:

Former Lady Vol Isabelle Harrison started for the Tempo and played 21 minutes. She scored eight points and converted 3-of-12 field goal attempts and 2-of-2 free throw attempts. Harrison also recorded seven rebounds, two assists, two steals and two blocks.

Former Lady Vol Mercedes Russell did not play for the Fever due to a coach's decision.

Indiana's Kelsey Mitchell (29) and Caitlin Clark (24) led all scorers in the contest. Clark also totaled seven assists and three rebounds.

Marina Mabrey led Toronto in scoring with 22 points.

Indiana led for 97 percent of the contest and the Fever's largest lead was 17 points.

title: Dak Prescott caught in heated exchange as Cowboys-Saints practice brawl erupts
description: Dak Prescott was caught up in a chaotic, fight-filled joint practice between the Cowboys and Saints, with multiple brawls breaking out.
fullText:
Dak Prescott caught in heated exchange as Cowboys-Saints practice brawl erupts originally appeared on The Sporting News. Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here.

Joint practices are supposed to sharpen two rosters before the games actually count, giving coaches a look at competition beyond their own locker room. Tuesday's session between the Dallas Cowboys and New Orleans Saints in Oxnard turned into something closer to a fight card.

Quarterback Dak Prescott found himself in the middle of the chaos, visibly animated and gesturing at players from both sides as the practice spiraled through repeated skirmishes.

A roughly 31-second clip captured Prescott walking through groups of players, talking intensely and gesturing before what appeared to be a handshake with a Saints player. The video did not include clear audio, but reports describe him exchanging words with Saints edge rusher Chase Young during one of at least six separate altercations.

The clip, posted by The Athletic's Jon Machota with the caption "Dak Prescott not happy about something," quickly circulated among Cowboys and Saints fans reacting to the intensity.

The physical play started early, when Saints tight end Brock Rechsteiner, the son of WWE Hall of Famer Scott Steiner, body-slammed a Cowboys defender to the turf during one scuffle.

Cowboys outside linebacker Donovan Ezeiruaku was ejected for throwing punches, His second removal from a practice this offseason after a similar incident earlier in training camp.

"A little chippy," head coach Brian Schottenheimer told reporters. "Not the way we like to do business. Got to be better." He added, "We're certainly not going to take s- from anybody."

Safety Jalen Thompson offered a blunt take when asked whether the Cowboys came out ahead. Dallas' broader camp storylines this month, and Thompson's answer fit right in. "Of course we did," Thompson said. "Come on now."

Coaches Schottenheimer and Kellen Moore reportedly discussed ending the session early, before ultimately letting the teams work through the disruptions.

The two teams meet again in the preseason on August 28, giving both sides a chance to settle whatever carried over from Tuesday's session under actual game conditions.

title: Juventus Waiting in the Wings for Outgoing Milan Duo
description: Fikayo Tomori and Youssouf Fofana have already been excluded from the plans for next season while Milan work on their exits, and Juventus have shown interest in both, Sky reports.New Bianconeri direct...
fullText:
Fikayo Tomori and Youssouf Fofana have already been excluded from the plans for next season while Milan work on their exits, and Juventus have shown interest in both, Sky reports.

New Bianconeri director Fikayo Tomori helped bring the Englishman to San Siro a few years back. He'd be their top target either Federico Gatti or Lloyd Kelly were sold after the acquisition of Jhon Lucumi. The former was linked to Napoli, but they are signing Benoit Badiashile instead.

As with Tomori, Juventus have to make room before talking with Milan about Fofana. While Douglas Luiz has won over Luciano Spalletti, they haven't found a solution for Teun Koopmeiners and Fabio Miretti at this stage. A swap with fellow outcast Nicolas Gonzalez has been suggested. However, the Rossoneri have added Diego Moreira on the wings.

Christopher Nkunku and Santiago Gimenez are also on their way out. However, the offers from RB Leipzig and Porto have been deemed insufficient for now, especially because of the formula, a loan.

Rafael Leao's situation remains fluid, Fabrizio Romano reports (via Calciomercato). His agent, Jorge Mendes, is in Italy. Besides Galatasaray, Chelsea and some Saudi teams are tracking him.

The Rossoneri are naturally looking for sound terms but, since the duo has short-term contracts, they'll be lucky not to get squeezed. The hope is that maybe some second-tier Premier League sides with deep pockets that could give them starring roles will materialize. Instead, they'd have to fight for minutes in Turin. They'd be okay signings only if they were cheap. They don't really have a workhorse like the former in their squad, and he could help them pull off a very attacking formation.

title: Patriots’ roster crunch could be decided by Mike Vrabel’s ties to particular player
description: Connection to Mike Vrabel could save someone a roster spot.
fullText:
The New England Patriots are approaching one of the most important stretches of the preseason, with roster decisions beginning to take shape across the team. As the second week of preseason games arrives, several players are fighting for their NFL futures, and the running back position could feature one of the more interesting battles.

For New England, Rhamondre Stevenson and TreVeyon Henderson appear to have the top two running back spots secured. That leaves the competition for RB3, and one player who wasn't even in the conversation a short time ago is suddenly making a strong push.

MORE: 5 most improved NFL offenses entering 2026-2027 season

Jul 28, 2026; Foxborough, MA, USA; New England Patriots head coach Mike Vrabel coaches the team during training camp at Gillette Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Eric Canha-Imagn Images Credit: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect (Reuters)

For much of the offseason, Jam Miller and Lars Larison appeared to be the primary candidates competing for the third running back job.

Then Patriots head coach Mike Vrabel made a move that changed the equation.

New England signed Hassan Haskins, a player Vrabel is already very familiar with. Vrabel was the head coach of the Tennessee Titans when the organization selected Haskins in the 2022 NFL Draft.

Haskins doesn't enter New England with an impressive statistical résumé. Over three seasons with two different teams, he has accumulated just 228 career rushing yards.

Yet despite that limited production, Haskins has quickly moved up the depth chart.

MORE: Predicting the AFC playoff teams ahead of the 2026-2027 NFL season

Feb 5, 2026; Santa Clara, CA, USA; New England Patriots head coach Mike Vrabel talks to media members at the Santa Clara Marriott. Mandatory Credit: Darren Yamashita-Imagn Images

The situation became even more interesting heading into Saturday's preseason matchup against the Philadelphia Eagles.

Haskins is now getting first-team reps, a significant development considering he only joined the Patriots last week. That could be a sign that Vrabel wants to get a closer look at a player he already knows before making the final decision on the running back room.

Haskins made his Patriots debut against the Colts last week, carrying the ball five times for 15 yards. New England is expected to give him an increased workload against Philadelphia, providing another opportunity for him to show the coaching staff that he belongs.

This isn't the first time Vrabel has shown a willingness to bring in players he previously coached. During the offseason, the Patriots traded for A.J. Brown, whom Vrabel coached during his time in Tennessee.

MORE: 4 NFL players with most pressure entering 2026-2027 season

There is still time for Miller and Larison to make their case, but the momentum appears to be shifting toward Haskins.

His familiarity with Vrabel's coaching style and the fact that the head coach already knows what he can bring to a team could give him an advantage in a competition where the margins are extremely thin.

If Haskins continues receiving first-team opportunities and performs well against the Eagles, don't be surprised if he goes from a late offseason addition to the Patriots' RB3 when the team breaks training camp.
